title: Slack Mailchimp Integration: How to Set It Up (2026)
summary: Slack Mailchimp integration automates workflows between the two apps without writing code. Choose the right no-code tool and follow the setup steps.
body_markdown:
## Building one Slack Mailchimp workflow step by step in Activepieces


Without writing any code, you can build and publish the gap-filling steps inside one short workflow in[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/mailchimp) : a single Mailchimp trigger feeding a single Slack action.


Activepieces has an MIT-licensed core, with its enterprise directories under a separate commercial licence in the same repository, and it can be self-hosted, so the same build runs on your own server if the subscriber data shouldn't pass through a hosted service.


If the Slack or Mailchimp step you need isn't in the catalogue, you don't wait on a vendor release: you can have AI generate the missing integration and keep it private to your own instance.


The catalogue stands at **750 integrations** , a count taken straight from the packages/integrations/community directory of the public GitHub monorepo rather than a figure published for marketing, and roughly 60% of them were contributed by the community rather than the vendor, which means you're unlikely to need custom integration code.


Eight steps make up the whole build, in order, and each stage after the list explains the step that most often goes wrong, by the time you're stuck you already know the most likely culprit.


1. Create a new flow.
2. Pick the Mailchimp trigger Member Subscribed to Audience.
3. Connect your Mailchimp account.
4. Add the Slack action Send Message To A Channel.
5. Connect your Slack workspace.
6. Map the trigger's fields into the message.
7. Test the flow.
8. Publish it.


Start a blank flow and choose Mailchimp as the trigger. The[Activepieces Mailchimp piece](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/mailchimp) lists nine triggers, including Member Subscribed to Audience, Member Unsubscribed from Audience, Link Clicked and Email Opened.


Pick Member Subscribed to Audience, then choose which audience it watches. If you have several audiences, this choice decides which signups ever reach Slack.


### Stage 2: connect Slack and Mailchimp


You will see two authorisation prompts: Mailchimp's in the trigger and Slack's in the action. Authorise Slack for the workspace where the channel lives.


If the message later fails to post, check that the app has access to that channel; private channels are the usual culprit.


### Stage 3: map the fields in the action


Add Slack's Send Message To A Channel, select the channel, and write the message text. Insert the subscriber's email address and name from the trigger's output instead of typing placeholders.


This is where the workflow earns its keep: a bare "new subscriber" ping tells the team nothing, while one carrying the address lets them act on it. Map only what the trigger returns, and open the sample data to see what that is.


### Stage 4: test, then publish


Run the trigger test first so Activepieces loads a real sample from your audience. Then test the Slack step and confirm the message lands in the right channel with the fields filled in, not blank.


A blank field here means the mapping points at data the trigger didn't return.


Once the message reads correctly, publish. **An unpublished flow only runs when you test it, so subscribers will arrive and nobody will be told.**
